source_caption:
Scarlett Johansson’s pivotal role as the tragic Nola Rice in Match Point almost didn’t happen. She was hired on a mere week’s notice to replace Kate Winslet, who had abruptly dropped out of the project for personal reasons. Johansson arrived on the London set without having previously met director Woody Allen or any of her co-stars. On her very first day of filming, she was immediately thrown into the deep end, forced to shoot a crucial, emotionally complex scene with Jonathan Rhys Meyers that spanned five pages of dialogue. Despite her initial nerves and a self-described “horrible” first take, she so deeply impressed the notoriously hands-off director that he offered her a starring role in his next film, Scoop, before Match Point had even wrapped production.

Match Point (2005), directed by Woody Allen, starring Jonathan Rhys Meyers, Scarlett Johansson, Emily Mortimer, Matthew Goode. A former tennis professional marries into a wealthy British family to elevate his social status, but his entire comfortable new life is jeopardized when he engages in a passionate, illicit affair with his brother-in-law’s American fiancée.

source_details.synopsis: Match Point is a 2005 psychological thriller film written and directed by Woody Allen, and starring Jonathan Rhys Meyers, Scarlett Johansson, Emily Mortimer, Matthew Goode, Brian Cox, and Penelope Wilton. In the film, Rhys Meyers' character, a former professional tennis player, marries into a wealthy family, but his social position is threatened by his affair with his brother-in-law's girlfriend, played by Scarlett Johansson. The film deals with themes of morality and greed, and explores the roles of lust, money, and luck in life, leading many to compare it to Allen's earlier film Crimes and Misdemeanors (1989).
